organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae PDC1/5/6; Zymomonas mobilis pdc; widespread in fungi, plants and fermentative bacteria
rationale: KEGG R00224 (EC 4.1.1.1) is plain ThDP-dependent pyruvate decarboxylase, a single catalytic activity; its acyloin/carboligase side reaction is active-site promiscuity at the same ThDP centre, not a second domain. Called from established knowledge plus the KEGG entry (COMMENT: 'TPP-dependent enzymatic reaction').
direction_note: ModelSEED carries an orphan ADP on the pyruvate side (status MI:C:-10/H:-12/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2 = one ADP, CI:3); that phantom nucleotide is what inflates dG to ~450 kJ/mol and produces the reverse call, while the real decarboxylation is irreversible forward.

organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Aro10p (Ehrlich pathway); Azospirillum/Enterobacter ipdC-type decarboxylases; KEGG ortholog K12732
rationale: KEGG R01377 (EC 4.1.1.43 / 4.1.1.-, ortholog K12732 'phenylpyruvate decarboxylase') is a single-activity ThDP decarboxylase of the PDC/IPDC family; no fused second catalytic domain is described for this family. Identity taken from the KEGG ortholog assignment rather than a dedicated characterisation paper.
direction_note: Same orphan-ADP artefact as rxn31646 (MI = one ADP); CO2-releasing 2-oxo-acid decarboxylation does not run backwards.

organism_context: Fungal (Agaricus bisporus PPO), plant and animal (mammalian TYR) tyrosinases; KEGG assigns ortholog K00505 (tyrosinase) to R02383, COMMENT 'tyramine monooxygenase'
rationale: The ModelSEED name is literally the EC 1.14.18.1 systematic name and KEGG maps R02383 to tyrosinase; a single tyrosinase polypeptide carries two distinct catalytic activities at one binuclear-copper centre - hydroxylation of monophenols and two-electron oxidation of o-diphenols to quinones. Bifunctional by catalysis, not by moonlighting; the two activities are routinely assayed and inhibited separately.
direction_note: Both tyrosinase activities are O2-consuming oxidations, so the reverse direction would require the enzyme to evolve O2 - impossible; the reverse call comes from the orphan ADP (MI = one ADP) inflating dG, and NADH here is only a balancing stand-in for the o-diphenol that actually reduces the copper centre.

organism_context: KEGG places R02669 in tryptophan metabolism (rn00380); fungal 3-hydroxyanthranilate branches (e.g. Aspergillus terreus salicylate catabolism) are the usual context
rationale: KEGG R02669 carries only the unassigned EC 4.1.1.-, no ORTHOLOGY entry and no COMMENT, and no characterised protein for 3-hydroxyanthranilate -> 2-aminophenol + CO2 surfaced in the literature search. Honest 'unknown' rather than a guessed mono call.
direction_note: Orphan ADP again (MI = one ADP, CI:3); whichever protein runs it, aromatic decarboxylation with CO2 release is the biologically observed direction.

organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Coq7p (hexaprenyl chain = Q6, matching the substrate named here); C. elegans CLK-1; a flavin-dependent DMQ hydroxylase substitutes in Arabidopsis and UbiF in E. coli
rationale: The C5 hydroxylation of 2-hexaprenyl-3-methyl-6-methoxy-1,4-benzoquinone is diagnostically the Coq7 step of Q6 biosynthesis; Coq7/CLK-1 is a single carboxylate-bridged di-iron monooxygenase with one catalytic activity. Enzyme identity inferred from the chemistry and prenyl-chain length - KEGG no longer serves R04984 (the entry returns empty), so there is no ortholog assignment to confirm against.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI:C:-10/H:-13/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2, CI:2) drives the reverse call; an O2/NAD(P)H-consuming hydroxylation is irreversible forward.

organism_context: Escherichia coli UbiD (octaprenyl chain matches); prFMN cofactor is supplied in trans by the separate flavin prenyltransferase UbiX (EC 2.5.1.129, KEGG K03186)
rationale: KEGG R04986 assigns EC 4.1.1.98 / K03182 (UbiD). UbiD carries one catalytic activity; UbiX is a distinct polypeptide that only matures the prFMN cofactor, so this is a two-protein cofactor relationship, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: prFMN/UbiD-family decarboxylases are mechanistically reversible and some relatives run as carboxylases in anaerobes, but in ubiquinone biosynthesis UbiD runs decarboxylation; the reverse call here is an artefact of the orphan ADP (MI = one ADP).

enzyme_name: OhpA, self-sufficient cytochrome P450 of the CYP116B subfamily (2-hydroxyphenylacetate 5-hydroxylase)
organism_context: Cupriavidus pinatubonensis JMP134; homologues across Actinobacteria and alpha-/beta-/gamma-proteobacteria
rationale: Donoso et al. showed OhpA, a CYP116B 'self-sufficient' P450, converts 2-hydroxyphenylacetate to homogentisate, matching KEGG R05450 ('2-hydroxy-phenylacetate hydroxylase'). The chain is a natural fusion of a P450 heme domain with an FMN/2Fe-2S reductase module, but that module only delivers electrons internally to the same oxidation - one metabolic activity, so monofunctional rather than bifunctional.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI = one ADP) is the source of the +360/+250 kJ/mol values; O2-consuming aromatic hydroxylation only runs forward.

organism_context: Aspergillus nidulans phacA (KEGG K10437); the related phacB P450 of the same organism hydroxylates 3-hydroxy- and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetate
rationale: Mingot et al. identified phacA as the A. nidulans P450 catalysing phenylacetate 2-hydroxylation, exactly KEGG R05487. A single P450 heme monooxygenase activity; its broadened substrate range (phacB) is substrate promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Besides the orphan ADP (MI = one ADP), ModelSEED replaces KEGG's [reduced NADPH-hemoprotein reductase] partner with free NADH; either way an O2-consuming P450 hydroxylation cannot run in reverse.

enzyme_name: StyA, styrene monooxygenase oxygenase component (EC 1.14.14.11), with StyB reductase
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. VLB120 / P. fluorescens ST styAB (KEGG K14481 + K14482); natural single-chain fusions (StyA2B) occur in Rhodococcus and Variovorax paradoxus
rationale: This is the classic two-component flavoprotein monooxygenase: StyA epoxidises styrene using FADH2, StyB is a separate NAD(P)H:FAD reductase polypeptide. Per the multi-subunit exclusion the epoxidising subunit StyA is monofunctional; only the lineage-restricted StyA2B fusions put both activities on one chain.
direction_note: The worst-corrupted entry in this chunk: three orphan ADP (MI:C:-30/H:-36/N:-15/O:-30/P:-6, CI:7) and FAD/FADH2 written on the wrong sides relative to KEGG R05488, where FADH2 is the reductant consumed; the ~+1000 to +1290 kJ/mol driving the reverse call is pure artefact.

organism_context: Fused IspDF single chain in Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori and other alpha-/epsilon-proteobacteria (KEGG K12506); separate monofunctional IspD and IspF in E. coli and plants (K00991)
rationale: KEGG R05633 is assigned both to monofunctional IspD (K00991) and to the fused bifunctional IspDF (K12506), and Lherbet et al. characterised the A. tumefaciens IspDF chain carrying both the cytidylyltransferase and the cyclodiphosphate synthase active sites (they showed no substrate channelling between them). Bifunctional in some lineages, which the protocol counts as bifunctional.
direction_note: The IspD half-reaction is near-equilibrium in vitro; in vivo it is pulled forward by PPi hydrolysis and by the consuming IspF step - which in IspDF sits on the same polypeptide - so forward is the physiological direction. The reverse call comes from the orphan ADP (MI = one ADP, CI:2).

organism_context: Activity demonstrated in whole cells and extracts of Arthrobacter sp. IF1 (4-fluorophenol catabolism) and in hydroxyquinol-pathway strains such as Rhodococcus jostii RHA1; fungal phenol 2-monooxygenases also hydroxylate hydroquinone
rationale: KEGG R06851 carries only EC 1.14.13.- with no ORTHOLOGY, and the literature establishes the hydroquinone -> hydroxyquinol conversion physiologically (Ferreira et al., Arthrobacter IF1) without naming the protein that performs it. No basis to call mono vs bi.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI = one ADP); an O2/NADPH-consuming ring hydroxylation is irreversible forward whatever the protein.

enzyme_name: 1-Methylnaphthalene methyl-group monooxygenase (uncharacterised cytochrome P450 / ring-and-methyl monooxygenase)
organism_context: Cunninghamella elegans (fungal cytochrome P450 route), Pseudomonas putida CSV86 (methyl-oxidation branch to 1-naphthoic acid); also a rat/trout hepatic P450 reaction
rationale: KEGG R06916 is only COMMENT '1-methylnaphthalene hydroxylase' with EC 1.14.13.- and no ortholog; the published work establishes the transformation in C. elegans and P. putida CSV86 without isolating the responsible monooxygenase. Cannot judge functionality.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI = one ADP); benzylic hydroxylation consuming O2 and NADH does not reverse.

organism_context: Cunninghamella elegans; Pseudomonas putida CSV86; mammalian hepatic microsomal P450s also form (2-naphthyl)methanol from 2-methylnaphthalene
rationale: KEGG R06926 gives only COMMENT '2-methylnaphthalene hydroxylase', EC 1.14.13.-, no ortholog; the transformation is documented in fungal and bacterial whole-cell studies and in purified mammalian P450 preparations, but no single catalysing protein is assigned to this entry.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI = one ADP) drives the reverse call; the real reaction is an irreversible O2-consuming benzylic hydroxylation.

organism_context: Pseudomonas pavonaceae 170 and Coryneform bacterium strain FG41, 1,3-dichloropropene catabolism; KEGG ortholog K14422
rationale: KEGG R06973 names MSAD directly. Guo et al. report MSAD has 'two known activities' - the physiological metal-independent decarboxylation and a low-level hydration of 2-oxo-3-pentynoate that is explicitly 'not known to be biologically relevant' - so the second is active-site promiscuity at the same Pro-1 centre, not a second physiological catalytic function; monofunctional.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI = one ADP, CI:3). Note KEGG also attaches this overall transformation to a four-step (methylthio)acryloyl-CoA hydratase route (EC 4.2.1.155, 'see R10936, R10945+R10946+R10947+R06973'), but via MSAD it is a single irreversible decarboxylation.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and other plants/cyanobacteria, plastoquinone-9 biosynthesis; KEGG ortholog K12501, EC 2.5.1.117; herbicide target of cyclopyrimorate
rationale: KEGG R08782 maps to K12501 (homogentisate solanesyltransferase) and Sadre et al. dissected its catalytic reactions. Prenylation and the accompanying decarboxylation are one concerted catalytic event at a single UbiA-fold active site, not two separable activities, so monofunctional.
direction_note: Orphan ADP (MI:C:-10/H:-13/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2, CI:2); the real reaction releases both CO2 and PPi and is committed-step irreversible.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana ACX1/ACX5 and tomato ACX1A; peroxisomal beta-oxidation of OPC-8:0 in jasmonate biosynthesis
rationale: The OPC6-CoA dehydrogenation step of jasmonate biosynthesis is run by the long/medium-chain acyl-CoA oxidase ACX1, a single FAD-dependent oxidase (crystal structure solved for tomato ACX1); the multifunctional protein of plant beta-oxidation (MFP2/AIM1) carries the next steps, not this one.
direction_note: ACX reoxidises its enzyme-bound FAD with O2 to H2O2, which is exactly what makes the step irreversible; ModelSEED substitutes free FAD/FADH2 and drops O2/H2O2, leaving a near-equilibrium couple (eQuilibrator +18.9 kJ/mol) that produces the spurious reverse call.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana ACX1 (the OPC-8:0-preferring isoform) and tomato ACX1A; peroxisomal jasmonate beta-oxidation
rationale: First round of OPC-8:0 beta-oxidation; ACX1 is the acyl-CoA oxidase shown genetically and biochemically to act on OPC-8:0-CoA, and it is a single-activity FAD oxidase, not a multifunctional protein.
direction_note: Same defect as rxn31879: free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the enzyme-bound flavin and the O2 -> H2O2 half-reaction that enforces irreversibility is absent from the equation.

enzyme_name: Unidentified oxidoreductase of the coumestan (coumestrol) branch; 2'-hydroxydaidzein ring rearrangement
organism_context: Glycine max (soybean) and other legumes; coumestrol biosynthesis
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-10866 carries no EC in ModelSEED and the coumestrol pathway is explicitly incomplete - Ha et al. could only nominate candidate oxidoreductase genes by co-expression, and the pterocarpan/coumestan review likewise lists the oxidative steps as uncharacterised. No protein to classify.
direction_note: Written as a hydration releasing 2 H+ (ModelSEED status CI:2), i.e. a two-electron oxidation with no oxidant in the equation; biosynthesis runs isoflavone -> coumestan, so the forward sense is right even though the thermodynamics as written are meaningless.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana ACX1/ACX5 (shorter-chain rounds), tomato ACX1A; final beta-oxidation round of jasmonate biosynthesis
rationale: Third beta-oxidation round of OPC-8:0; the dehydrogenation is run by the same monofunctional FAD-dependent acyl-CoA oxidase family (ACX1, with ACX5 contributing at shorter chain lengths), each a single-activity enzyme.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 replaces the bound flavin and the O2/H2O2 couple is missing, removing the thermodynamic driving force that makes the oxidase step one-way.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana; SOT16 is the isoform preferring indolic (tryptophan-derived) desulfoglucosinolates, SOT17/SOT18 prefer long-chain aliphatic ones
rationale: Klein et al. characterised the three Arabidopsis desulfoglucosinolate sulfotransferases and showed SOT16 is the indolic-substrate isoform, matching this indolylmethyl substrate; cytosolic plant SOTs are single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: ModelSEED status MI:C:-6/H:-12/O:-5 - a whole glucosyl unit is lost between substrate and product naming - and PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is in any case effectively irreversible at cellular PAPS/PAP ratios.

organism_context: Aspergillus flavus quercitrinase (the EC 3.2.1.66 type enzyme); GH78 alpha-L-rhamnosidases of human gut bacteria and fungi hydrolyse quercitrin equivalently
rationale: The transformation is a single alpha-L-rhamnoside hydrolysis; GH78/quercitrinase-type rhamnosidases are single-catalytic-activity glycoside hydrolases (multi-domain, but only one glycosidase active site). Family-level call rather than a characterisation of one specific protein.
direction_note: ModelSEED status CI:-2: a spurious H+ sits on the substrate side, which at pH 7 adds roughly +40 kJ/mol to dG'0 - essentially all of eQuilibrator's +41.3 and the entire basis for the reverse call; glycoside hydrolysis is strongly exergonic forward.

enzyme_name: None - spontaneous (and light-catalysed) lactonization of cis-2,4-dihydroxycinnamate to umbelliferone
organism_context: Plant coumarin biosynthesis; the enzymatic counterpart COSY (Arabidopsis COUMARIN SYNTHASE, a BAHD-family protein) acts on the CoA thioester, not on the free acid used here
rationale: ModelSEED assigns no EC to this MetaCyc entry, and Vanholme et al. state the trans-cis isomerization plus lactonization 'happens partially spontaneously and is catalysed by light'; the one enzyme known for it (COSY) uses o-hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA thioesters, so no enzyme catalyses the free-acid reaction as written.
direction_note: Lactone ring closure is strongly favoured at physiological pH and nothing drives umbelliferone back to the open hydroxycinnamate, so the forward sense is right - but since the step is non-enzymatic, no enzymology supports either flux bound.

enzyme_name: Unidentified oxidase/oxidoreductase of the coumestan branch; anhydroglycinol -> coumestrol
organism_context: Glycine max and other legumes; final oxidation of coumestrol biosynthesis
rationale: ModelSEED carries no EC and no name for this entry, and the coumestrol pathway's oxidative steps remain uncharacterised - the RNA-seq/co-expression study could only propose candidate oxidoreductases. Genuine unknown.
direction_note: The equation is a four-electron oxidation written as hydration releasing 4 H+ with no oxidant present (ModelSEED status CI:4); the biosynthetic sense is anhydroglycinol -> coumestrol, but the dG values for either direction are uninterpretable.

organism_context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii model entry (JM_Cre_34); single multidomain alpha4 chain in yeast, fungi, animals and most bacteria, but a two-subunit alpha/beta holoenzyme in some bacteria (e.g. Methanocaldococcus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
rationale: One EC, one overall transformation: the biotin carboxylase and carboxyltransferase domains run two halves of a single catalytic cycle joined by a covalently tethered carboxybiotin that never leaves the enzyme, so this is a multidomain monofunctional enzyme rather than a PFK2/FBPase2-style bifunctional one. In a subset of bacteria the same two domains sit on separate subunits, which the multi-subunit exclusion also treats as monofunctional.
direction_note: ModelSEED status MI:H:-2/O:-4/P:-1 - the Pi product is missing from the equation, which is what produces the absurd +247 to +270 kJ/mol; ATP hydrolysis makes carboxylation strongly forward and pyruvate carboxylase has no physiological decarboxylating role (that belongs to PEPCK and malic enzyme).

enzyme_name: F1F0-ATP synthase (mitochondrial Complex V); catalytic beta subunit
organism_context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii mitochondrial model entry (JM_Cre_145); F1F0 rotary ATP synthase is conserved across mitochondria, chloroplasts and bacteria
rationale: ATP synthase is a ~17-subunit rotary complex, not a fused chain, so per the multi-subunit exclusion the catalytic beta subunit that performs ATP synthesis/hydrolysis is monofunctional. Called from established knowledge; the listed EC 3.6.3.6 is the pre-2018 numbering, superseded by the EC 7.1.2.x translocase class.
direction_note: Direction is set by the proton-motive force, not by the protein: F1F0 synthesises ATP in respiring mitochondria (the council's forward sense) and runs as a proton-pumping ATPase when the PMF collapses. The equation keeps only a single H+ inside one compartment and never moves protons across the membrane, so the energy partner that would fix a direction is absent entirely.
